title: Dynamic token-aware scaler and latency prober for embeddings ingress
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Build a token-aware autoscaling controller and a latency probing harness for the embeddings ingress path to reduce p99 tail latency and improve cost predictability under variable token-length workloads. Background: Embeddings traffic has highly variable token lengths (short queries, long documents, batched rerank flows) that cause autoscalers tuned on QPS or request-count to either overprovision for worst-case or underprovision and spike p99 latency. We need a controller that reasons in token-seconds and a probing system that continuously validates p99 SLOs across tenant mixes and model variants. Scope: 1) A simulator that replays sampled production token-length distributions (stratified by tenant and route) and exposes metrics (tokens/sec, effective batch size, GPU utilization, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency). 2) A token-aware autoscaler that consumes simulator-derived policies and live telemetry to make scaling decisions in token-seconds and target buffer headroom. 3) A lightweight latency prober that issues synthetic requests (short/medium/long tokens + batch shapes) at low rate to detect emergent tail behavior and trigger conservative scale-ups. 4) Integration with per-tenant rate-shaper so that scaling decisions are tenant-aware and soft-throttles can be applied before hard drops. Out of scope: major rewrite of the Serving runtime kernels or quantization changes; those are follow-ups if we find model-level bottlenecks. Design notes: - Token accounting: convert each inbound request into token-weighted units (estimated tokens * concurrency weight) and use a short-lived moving window (60s/5s granularity) to derive token-s/sec. - Autoscaling policy: combine a baseline target GPU tokens/sec capacity plus a headroom multiplier that depends on observed tail variance from the latency prober. - Queue resizer: adapt per-route leaky-bucket token capacity so that queueing delay is bounded; allow short bursts when GPU has slack but gracefully degrade by serving lower-cost quantized model variant if latency crosses thresholds. - Prober behavior: low-rate synthetic sampling across token-length strata; measures 95/99/99.9 latencies, KV cache effectiveness (simulated), and effective batch sizes. - Simulator: replay with stochastic jitter and tenant mix permutations. It must be fast to run locally and on CI for policy validation. Trade-offs considered: - Decision granularity: token-seconds lets us reason about cost better but adds complexity to billing/observability pipelines. We're starting with internal-only token accounting surfaced in Console; billing integration is a follow-up. - Reactive vs predictive: initial controller is reactive with conservative headroom based on recent prober signals; predictive forecasting (AR/ML) is a separate workstream. - Soft-throttle vs immediate scale: prefer soft-shaping to avoid oscillation and to protect high-priority tenants. Rollout plan: 1) Build simulator and run replay experiments on last 30 days of anonymized token logs (internal only) (2 weeks). 2) Implement prober and integrate metrics into dashboards (2 weeks). 3) Implement token-aware scaler as an opt-in policy for a small set of internal tenants and QA canaries (3 weeks). 4) Gradual ramp to broader tenants with monitoring and automatic rollback criteria (2 weeks). Metrics and success criteria: - Reduce embeddings p99 latency by >= 20% on canary tenants under identical load patterns. - Maintain GPU utilization >= 60% while reducing overprovisioning cost by 15% vs existing QPS autoscaler on median week. - False-positive scale-ups (unnecessary scale events) under 5% per day. - No more than 0.5% increased throttled requests during ramp. Observability: - New dashboard panels: token/sec by tenant/route, effective batch size distribution, queue depth percentiles, autoscale decisions timeline, prober latency timeline. - Alerting: sustained p99 > SLO for 5m triggers traffic hold and automated rollback; surge of scale activities (more than 3 scale events in 15m) triggers operator review. Acceptance criteria: - Simulator can reproduce p99 behavior observed in at least two historical incidents. - Prober detects regressions injected in canary (we'll introduce synthetic 30% latency regression and expect prober to catch it within 5 minutes). - Token-aware scaler runs in opt-in mode and demonstrates controlled scale-ups without oscillation for at least 48 hours in staging. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: inaccurate token estimation for languages/tokenizers -> Mitigate by validating token estimates using sampled production traces and exposing confidence bands. - Risk: tenant weight misconfiguration causes unfair degradation -> Mitigate by defaulting to tenant-preserving weights and requiring explicit opt-in for experimental policies. - Risk: oscillation between scaling and soft-throttle -> Mitigate with cooldown windows and hysteresis. Security/privacy: simulator and prober run on anonymized logs; no raw customer data leaves infra. Implementation notes and interfaces: - New metric names: embeddings.tokens_per_sec, embeddings.effective_batch_size, embeddings.queue_depth_pctile, embeddings.scale_decision_reason. - Autoscaler config flags: enabled (bool), headroom_multiplier (float), token_window_seconds (int), prober_enabled (bool), tenant_weight_overrides (map) [map surfaced via Console UI; internal API will accept JSON string]. - Console: add rollout toggle and realtime view for canary tenants. Deliverables: - simulator service + test harness (Go/Python) - prober library (small service) and instrumented probes - autoscaler implementation (controller) + unit/integration tests - Console panels and alerting rules - Runbook for operators with rollback steps and postmortem template.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator reproduces p99 tail for two historical incidents within +/-10%
Prober detects injected 30% latency regression within 5 minutes in staging
Token-aware autoscaler runs in opt-in mode and shows stable behavior for 48h without oscillation
Canary tenants show >=20% p99 latency reduction under same load patterns
GPU utilization remains >=60% while cost reduces ~15% vs current autoscaler on median week
